parsed_payload.reasoning: Let O be the incenter and AB the given leg, with OA=5 and OB=12. Since the bases of the trapezoid are parallel, the two angles at A and B adjacent to leg AB are supplementary: \(\alpha+\beta=180^\circ\). Because O is the incenter, AO and BO bisect these angles, so \(\angle OAB=\alpha/2\) and \(\angle OBA=\beta/2\). Thus in triangle AOB, \(\angle AOB=180^\circ-(\alpha/2+\beta/2)=180^\circ-90^\circ=90^\circ\). Therefore triangle AOB is right at O with legs OA=5 and OB=12. By the Pythagorean theorem, \(AB=\sqrt{5^2+12^2}=\sqrt{25+144}=\sqrt{169}=13\). Hence the length of the side is \boxed{13}.

However, The solution assumes the incenter O lies on leg AB and therefore adds OA and OB to get AB. In fact O is inside the trapezoid, not on the side, so AB is the third side of triangle AOB, not the sum of OA and OB.
Next, Use the fact that in a trapezoid the two angles adjacent to leg AB are supplementary, so their angle bisectors AO and BO meet at a right angle; then triangle AOB is right at O and AB is found by the Pythagorean theorem.
</reflection>
